summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to permit and log TCP/23 traffic from node3 to node4, and node2 (OPNsense) to reject and log the same flow, using a forced next-hop chain (node3 -> node1 -> node2) since all four nodes share one flat /24 with a single NIC each. Verified with a live attempt from node3 that produces a correlated pair of log entries (matching IP-ID/source-port) showing the SYN packet permitted at node1 and refused at node2, proving that is where the traffic stops. All four nodes were then restarted one at a time via native reboot, boot identity change confirmed on each, and node1/node2 firewall configuration was proven to persist across reboot; the demo was re-run post-restart producing a fresh matching log pair.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=VyOS, node2=OPNsense (FreeBSD/pf), node3/node4=RHEL9, all single-NIC on one flat 10.100.40.0/24 subnet
Added host route on node3 (10.100.40.13/32 via node1) so traffic to node4 traverses node1 first
On node1 (VyOS): added static route 10.100.40.13/32 next-hop node2, and firewall ipv4 forward filter rule 10 (accept + log) matching tcp/23 to node4; committed and saved
On node2 (OPNsense): inserted a reject+log filter rule (tcp/23 to node4) ahead of the default-allow rules in config.xml, then ran configctl filter reload
Started a socat listener on node4:23 as the nominal target service

From node3, attempted a TCP connection to node4:23; got Connection refused; pulled the correlated log pair from node1 (kernel netfilter log, ACCEPT) and node2 (pf filterlog, block) showing the identical packet (matching IP ID / source port)
Captured healthy baseline (boot identity + config state) on all four nodes

Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time via native reboot; for each, confirmed the node went unreachable, polled until exec access returned, and confirmed a changed boot identity (boot_id or kern.boottime)
Verified node1's firewall/static-route config and node2's reject/log rule both persisted across their respective reboots

Re-added node3's ephemeral host route and node4's socat listener (both non-persistent by nature) after restart, then re-ran the node3->node4 attempt to produce a fresh, current correlated log pair confirming the same permit-at-node1/refuse-at-node2 behavior post-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 permits the node3->node4 tcp/23 traffic and records it
evidence.summary: VyOS forward-filter rule 10 (action accept, log) plus static route via node2 were committed/saved; kernel log shows [ipv4-FWD-filter-10-A] ACCEPT entries for SRC=10.100.40.12 DST=10.100.40.13 DPT=23 SYN, both on the initial attempt and the post-restart attempt.

evidence.requirement: node2 refuses the same traffic and records the refusal
evidence.summary: OPNsense config.xml reject+log rule for tcp/23 to 10.100.40.13 inserted ahead of default-allow and applied via configctl filter reload; pf filterlog shows block entries for the same flow on both the initial and post-restart attempts.

evidence.requirement: Show the pair of log entries from one attempt demonstrating where traffic stopped
evidence.summary: Post-restart attempt from node3 (Connection refused) is captured by both routers with matching packet identifiers (IP ID=1116, source port=51802): node1 logs ACCEPT, node2 logs block -- proving the traffic passed node1 and stopped at node2.

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS) restart with boot-identity proof and recovered config
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 01e92881...; reboot issued; node unreachable; new boot_id 9646a54a... after recovery; forward-filter rule 10 and static route confirmed still present post-reboot.

evidence.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) restart with boot-identity proof and recovered config
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime 05:55:41; reboot issued; SSH transport unreachable; new kern.boottime 06:01:48 after recovery; reject+log rule confirmed still present in config.xml and active in pf ruleset post-reboot.

evidence.requirement: node3 (RHEL9) restart with boot-identity proof and recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 555221a1...; reboot issued; node unreachable; new boot_id fbcc29f5... after recovery; host route re-established and node basic network reachability confirmed.

evidence.requirement: node4 (RHEL9) restart with boot-identity proof and recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 34027437...; reboot issued; node unreachable; new boot_id 9d3e0db1... after recovery; port-23 listener re-established confirming service recovery.
